reason: The proof uses the standard fact that a continuous map has closed inverse images of closed sets; the supplied proof is correct, with the closedness of \(\{0\}\subseteq\mathbb R\) made explicit.
text:
Since \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\), the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). But
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\}).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.
